title: Linear Algebra
description: Vectors, matrices, determinants, eigenvalues and bases.

questions.text: What is the dot product of (1, 2, 3) and (4, 5, 6)?
What is the determinant of the matrix [[1, 2], [3, 4]]?
questions.explanation: For [[a, b], [c, d]] the determinant is ad − bc = 4 − 6 = −2.

questions.text: If A is 2 × 3 and B is 3 × 4, what is the size of AB?
questions.explanation: The inner sizes (3) match, and the result takes the outer sizes: 2 × 4.

questions.text: What does the identity matrix look like?
choices: Ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere
questions.explanation: The identity matrix I has 1s on the main diagonal and satisfies AI = IA = A.

questions.text: A square matrix is invertible exactly when:
questions.explanation: A zero determinant means the columns are dependent and no inverse exists.

questions.text: What is the size of the transpose of a 3 × 2 matrix?
What is the length (norm) of the vector (3, 4)?
Two non-zero vectors are orthogonal when:
choices: One is a multiple of the other
questions.explanation: Orthogonal (perpendicular) vectors have a dot product of zero.

questions.text: What is an eigenvector of a matrix A?
choices: A vector whose entries are all equal
A non-zero vector v with Av = λv for some scalar λ
A vector orthogonal to every row of A
questions.explanation: A only stretches an eigenvector by its eigenvalue λ, without changing its direction.

questions.text: What are the eigenvalues of [[2, 0], [0, 3]]?
questions.explanation: The eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix are its diagonal entries.

questions.text: What is the rank of [[1, 2], [2, 4]]?
questions.explanation: The second row is twice the first, so only one row is linearly independent.

questions.text: What is the trace of [[5, 1], [2, 7]]?
questions.explanation: The trace is the sum of the main diagonal: 5 + 7 = 12.

questions.text: In general, matrix multiplication is:
choices: The same as multiplying entry by entry
questions.explanation: For most matrices AB and BA are different, and one of them may not even be defined.

questions.text: What is det(AB) for square matrices A and B?
questions.explanation: The determinant is multiplicative: det(AB) = det(A) det(B).

questions.text: What is (AB)ᵀ equal to?
questions.explanation: The transpose of a product reverses the order: (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ.

questions.text: What can be said about the vectors (1, 0) and (0, 1) in R²?
choices: They form a basis of R²
questions.explanation: They are independent and every vector (x, y) is x(1, 0) + y(0, 1).

questions.text: What is the dimension of R³?
questions.explanation: R³ has a basis of three vectors, for example (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1).

questions.text: What is the cross product (1, 0, 0) × (0, 1, 0)?
questions.explanation: i × j = k by the right-hand rule.

questions.text: Swapping two rows of a square matrix multiplies its determinant by:
questions.explanation: Each row swap flips the sign of the determinant.

questions.text: A set of vectors is linearly independent when:
choices: Their sum is the zero vector
They all have the same length
Only the all-zero combination of them gives the zero vector
questions.explanation: No vector in the set can be written as a combination of the others.
